Standalone box (PoE on -10/-20 SKUs; -00 is 5V DC), not a rack card. Also has 2x RS-232 + 6x IR control ports for source control. Receives up to 8 AVB streams from the network and can route any stream to any of the 8 stereo outputs (matrix-style, not fixed-assignment). Max 15W draw (PoE on -10 SKU; -00 is 5V DC) (fits 802.3af). Supports mute/volume/PEQ/mono-sum/up to 160ms delay per output, plus GPIO to trigger an external amp. Balanced version: see savant-pav-aombal8c. sonos-amp.notes: One stereo zone, 2 amplified channels. 125W/ch RMS @8Ω (0.1% THD), roughly doubles into 4Ω (4Ω minimum load) — GOTCHA: several retailers title the SKU '250W' (125x2 summed, not per-channel); don't let that inflate a per-channel power figure in capacity math. 1x HDMI **ARC** input (not eARC) for TV sound — note the Amp is 2-channel only, so even over ARC it plays TV audio as a stereo downmix, no Atmos object/height decoding (contrast with the Arc Ultra/Beam Gen 2 soundbars below, which DO decode Atmos because they have the driver array for it). 1x stereo RCA line-in (turntable/CD), shareable/groupable to play on other Sonos rooms subject to the same 75ms line-in buffering as the Port (see headline note above). Auto-detecting sub output, adjustable 50–110Hz crossover. Dual 10/100 Ethernet (NOT gigabit — irrelevant for the Amp's own low-bitrate audio stream, but a hard ceiling if daisy-chaining other gear off it) or WiFi. Each of the 2 channels can drive 2 pairs of 8Ω speakers wired in parallel (4Ω net) — i.e. up to 4 speakers total (2 pairs) off one Amp, but they're all ONE volume zone; a second physical area needing independent volume needs its own Amp or a volume-control speaker selector downstream. NO 70V/100V capability — confirmed absent from every spec source found; Sonos amps are low-Z consumer-grade only, never spec this for a 70V distributed run. AUDIT 2026-09-27: optical in only via the Sonos Optical Audio Adapter (sold separately) on the HDMI port. sonos-port.notes: Bidirectional bridge box, not just a one-way source: the SAME unit simultaneously (a) ingests a legacy analog source (turntable, CD player, an AVR's 2ch preout) via its 1x stereo RCA line-in and makes it available/groupable across the Sonos system, AND (b) decodes whatever the Sonos system is playing back out to a legacy zone amp/receiver via 1x stereo RCA line-out + 1x digital coax out (NO optical out — coax only). Also has a 12V trigger output (200mA) to power on a downstream amp, not counted in the port totals above. Dual 10/100 Ethernet, no PoE. LIP-SYNC GOTCHA (see headline note): minimum 75ms buffered latency on the line-in path the moment it's grouped with other rooms, by design, for multiroom sync — stacks with the TV's own ~100–150ms video-processing delay if used to encode TV audio. Sonos added Group Audio Delay + Audio Delay compensation settings in app/firmware 10.6.2 specifically for this; treat as 'viable with per-room tuning,' not 'automatically lip-synced out of the box.' No successor SKU found as of this research date — 'Port 2' appears to be unfounded/no active rumor (see Unresolved). avpro-ac-aex-dearc-kit.notes: TV audio back to the rack, audio only (no video). TX at the TV on its eARC HDMI port (DIP 2-3 = eARC); one Cat6A (Cat5e min, 100m) AP-LINK run; RX in the rack. RX DIP 2: 0 = eARC OUT (acts as a TV on an eARC port — on an AVR that's the HDMI out the video uses), 1 = HDMI OUT (audio-only HDMI into any receiver HDMI input) — SignalPath lands it on an HDMI input. eARC: PCM 2.0 / LPCM 5.1 & 7.1 / DD / DD+ / TrueHD / Atmos / DTS / DTS-HD MA / DTS:X; optical/ARC: PCM 2.0 / DD / DTS 5.1; analog 2.0. Does NOT downmix (set the TV to stereo for 2ch use). One 12V 2A PSU powers both ends over the cable (PoC); 24W max total. Bidirectional IR / RS-232 / CEC. avproglobal.com/products/ac-aex-dearc-kit + user manual, 2026-09-30
